calls.head: Good looks against hopeful ones
calls.body: On shot quality, St. Louis is one of the league’s best and Chicago is near the bottom of the league. That’s about as far apart as two teams get.
calls.call: The Blues’ shots are more dangerous on average than the Blackhawks’.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: On how dangerous the average shot was, St. Louis had 6.0% a shot and Chicago 4.0% a shot. Coming in, St. Louis was at 6.7% a shot and Chicago at 6.1% a shot.
calls.usual: STL 6.7% a shot · CHI 6.1% a shot
calls.tonight: STL 6.0% a shot · CHI 4.0% a shot
calls.beyond: Chicago’s shots at 5-on-5 were less dangerous than usual: a 4.0% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.1% (league average 6.3%). A team strays this far about once every 35 games.

calls.head: The Blues hit; the Blackhawks mostly don’t
calls.body: The Blues are around the middle of the league for physicality, at the bruising end; the Blackhawks are one of the league’s worst, at the finesse end. Expect that gap to show.
calls.call: The Blues hit more than the Blackhawks in the close stretches of the game.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: On hit score in close games (arena-adjusted, 100 is league average), St. Louis had hit score 132 and Chicago hit score 82. Coming in, St. Louis was at hit score 100 and Chicago at hit score 76.
calls.usual: STL hit score 100 · CHI hit score 76
calls.tonight: STL hit score 132 · CHI hit score 82
calls.beyond: St. Louis’s hit score in the close stretches of the game was 132, against their usual 100 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 6 games.

CHI.head: We gave Chicago a 39% chance, and Chicago proved us wrong.

STL.head: We gave St. Louis a 61% chance, but Chicago had other ideas.

surprises.head: Chicago won against the run of play
surprises.body: Played out 100 times with these chances, St. Louis wins 70. Chicago won anyway.

surprises.head: St. Louis tried a different line
surprises.body: C. McMichael, J. Berggren, M. McTavish played 10:48 together at 5-on-5, a trio that isn’t one of St. Louis’s usual lines.

story.head: The Blackhawks steal one
paras: Mason McTavish opened the scoring late in the first. Four different Blackhawks scored. Cole Smith scored the winner late in the third.

The Blues had the better of the play. Replay the chances a hundred times and the Blues win about seven in ten. By our Swing measure, Connor McMichael had the best night of anyone, even in a loss. The Blues tried a line they hadn’t used before: McMichael, Jonatan Berggren and McTavish, and it had a hand in both of their goals.

items.text: The Blackhawks won for the first time in four games.
Whether the Blues keep that line together at home against San Jose on Thursday.
